stories.headline: Gong Surpasses $500M ARR With 55%+ Growth as Enterprises Consolidate on Revenue AI Operating Systems
stories.summary: Gong announced in May 2026 its tenth consecutive quarter of accelerating growth, crossing $500M ARR at over 55% year-over-year — with half the Fortune 10 now as customers and million-dollar enterprise deals closing at an unprecedented pace. The company frames its Revenue AI Operating System as the consolidation point for enterprise sales workflows, with documented ROI including a 141% deal win rate improvement at Paycor. For D&B, this confirms that data-rich, context-specific AI platforms are winning over generic tools — and that embedding D&B's entity-resolved signals into Gong's Revenue Graph is a high-value partnership surface for the Prospecting and Account Intelligence agent archetypes.

stories.headline: Gong Launches 'Mission Big Dipper' — A New Agentic Execution Layer Built for Enterprise Revenue Teams
stories.summary: In late June 2026, Gong announced Mission Big Dipper, introducing a Revenue Harness agentic execution layer built on Agent Studio and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, designed specifically to solve the governance and context failures that cause generic AI tools to break in production. The launch directly targets the gap between enterprise AI ambition and deployment reality — emphasizing human-in-the-loop control and revenue-specific context as differentiators. This is a direct validation of D&B's 'Explainability First' positioning: Gong is explicitly saying generic agents fail, and domain-specific, governed, context-rich data layers win — exactly the role D&B's DUNS, Paydex, and corporate family trees are positioned to fill.

stories.headline: Apollo Acquires Pocus — Signal-Based Selling M&A Wave Accelerates GTM Stack Consolidation
stories.summary: Apollo's acquisition of Pocus, reported in July 2026, merges Apollo's contact database and outbound execution engine with Pocus's product-led signal intelligence and revenue orchestration capabilities — part of a broader consolidation wave that also includes Clari-Salesloft and ZoomInfo's expansion via Chorus. Bain & Company's 2026 M&A analysis confirms consolidation is accelerating in profitable software verticals where AI can enhance product differentiation. For D&B, this shrinking vendor landscape raises both urgency and opportunity: as point solutions merge, D&B's neutral, platform-agnostic entity resolution and commercial data layer becomes more valuable as the one common data substrate across all consolidated stacks.

stories.headline: Moody's Wins Two 2026 Risk Technology Awards — Credit Data Provider of the Year and Best Use of AI
stories.summary: Moody's has been recognized with two 2026 Risk Technology Awards, taking Credit Data Provider of the Year and Best Use of AI — a double win that signals the market is rewarding established data providers who can credibly demonstrate AI integration rather than pure AI-native startups. The recognition reinforces Moody's positioning as the benchmark for trusted, AI-enhanced commercial risk intelligence. For D&B, this is a direct competitive signal: Moody's is successfully branding its AI capabilities alongside its data credibility — the same narrative D&B must own in the commercial data and entity resolution space, particularly as D&B itself navigates its Clearlake-backed private-company transition under CEO Steve Tulenko.

stories.headline: B2B Buyers Now Complete 60–70% of Tech Research Before Talking to a Vendor — Agentic AI Accelerating the 'Dark Funnel'
stories.summary: MarketScale's July 2026 analysis of enterprise B2B buying behavior confirms that buyers complete 60–70% of their technology research before engaging any vendor rep — a figure that is being further accelerated by agentic AI systems that autonomously conduct supplier searches, compare specifications, and check pricing without human intermediaries. Digital Commerce 360 and Deloitte research published the same month warn that suppliers whose data architectures were built for search-engine optimization rather than machine-readable consumption face a growing discoverability gap as AI agents scale. For D&B, this is a structural tailwind: AI agents doing the buying need structured, trusted, entity-resolved business data to function — and D&B's 600M+ business records, corporate family trees, and DUNS identifiers are precisely the kind of machine-readable ground truth these agents depend on.

stories.headline: Alibaba Drops Qwen3.8-Max — 2.4 Trillion Parameters, Open Weights Incoming, Priced at a Fraction of Anthropic
stories.summary: Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Max on August 3, its largest model ever at 2.4 trillion parameters on a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture, with a 1M-token context window and claims of performance rivalling Anthropic's Claude Fable 5. Alibaba priced API access at roughly 40% of Claude Opus 5 for input tokens and committed to open-sourcing the weights within days — a strategic reversal after several recent flagship releases were kept proprietary. Coming just a week after Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, this marks a third consecutive major Chinese open-weight launch in rapid succession, intensifying pressure on closed-source Western labs and continuing to erode the pricing floor for frontier-grade inference — directly relevant to D&B's data-layer positioning, as cheaper capable models accelerate enterprise agentic adoption.

stories.headline: Big Tech AI Capex Crosses $1 Trillion Combined — Morgan Stanley Sees Ultimate Ceiling Near $1.4T
stories.summary: As of early August, cumulative 2026 capital spending plans from Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta have crossed the $1 trillion mark in aggregate, according to analysis following the latest earnings season. Morgan Stanley now estimates total AI infrastructure investment could ultimately reach around $1.4 trillion, while the market narrative is shifting decisively from GPU acquisition counts to 'tokens per watt per dollar' as the key efficiency metric. For D&B, the scale of infrastructure buildout confirms the agentic AI platform race is real and well-funded — validating the urgency of embedding D&B's data layer into the platforms that will run on top of it.

stories.headline: EU AI Act's 'Digital Omnibus' Deferral Quietly Shifts High-Risk Compliance Runway Beyond August 2026
stories.summary: While the EU AI Act's core August 2 deadline is now in force, a provisional 'Digital Omnibus' agreement reached in spring 2026 has deferred several high-risk system obligations — granting use-based high-risk AI systems additional time beyond the original August 2026 date. This creates a two-tier compliance reality: transparency duties (Article 50 — content labelling, chatbot disclosure) are fully live, but obligations covering AI in credit scoring, insurance pricing, and employment decisions have a longer runway under the deferral. For D&B, whose data feeds AI systems making exactly these decisions, the deferral buys breathing room for customers but also raises the explainability and audit-trail bar that D&B's Ground Truth positioning directly addresses.

stories.headline: Asana Acquires StackAI and Autodesk Eyes MaintainX — Workflow SaaS Giants Race to Bundle Agentic AI
stories.summary: Asana completed its acquisition of AI workflow startup StackAI on July 31, adding multi-system integration and visualization capabilities to its AI Studio product, while Autodesk announced plans on August 2 to acquire maintenance-software firm MaintainX to deepen its own AI capabilities. Both deals reflect the same pattern: established SaaS platforms buying AI-native startups rather than building autonomously, compressing the window in which pure-play AI workflow vendors can operate independently. For D&B, this consolidation dynamic is a double-edged signal — fewer independent agentic platform bets to partner with, but growing urgency for the Salesforce Agentforce, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Copilot embedding strategy as the platforms absorbing these startups become the de facto agentic layer.

stories.headline: Burnham Faces First Major Test as Morocco Border Crisis Strains EU Solidarity
stories.summary: New PM Andy Burnham, who took office pledging to be a 'circuit-breaker' for Britain, faces an early foreign policy challenge as an unprecedented single-day migrant crossing into a Spanish EU exclave has destabilised Spain's domestic politics and tested EU solidarity mechanisms. The episode is feeding far-right momentum across Europe and puts pressure on Burnham's government to define its post-Starmer relationship with Brussels at a sensitive moment.

stories.headline: Trump Claims Iran Deal 'Perimeters Agreed' — But Tehran Has Not Confirmed Terms
stories.summary: President Trump declared that Iran and other Middle Eastern nations asked the US to hold off further military action because the parameters of a deal had been agreed, but Iranian officials including Foreign Minister Araghchi have not confirmed the deal's terms. With 40 US refuelling aircraft still in the region and the IRGC threatening 'decisive' retaliation for further strikes, the ceasefire remains unverified and fragile.

stories.headline: NASA's Curiosity Spots Honeycomb Shapes on Mars — and Roman Telescope Launch Countdown Begins
stories.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover has spotted surprising honeycomb-like shapes in Martian soil while exploring a large valley, adding to the list of unexplained surface formations on the Red Planet. Separately, NASA has confirmed its next major mission — the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope — is on track to launch on 30 August 2026 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center, where it is expected to discover around 100,000 exoplanets.

stories.headline: LIV Golf Plays at Bedminster as PGA Tour Heads Into August Quiet Period
stories.summary: The PGA Tour is currently in a quiet stretch of its schedule, with its next significant action coming in the weeks ahead. LIV Golf held its latest event at Trump National Bedminster this week. The DP World Tour resumes action on 13–16 August with the Danish Golf Championship, where Marco Penge is the defending champion.

stories.headline: Newcastle's £69.3m Barcelona Sale Shapes Summer Window — With Deadline Day Still Weeks Away
stories.summary: Newcastle United completed a £69.3m sale of a player to Barcelona in July, one of the biggest deals in the summer window so far. The Premier League transfer window, which opened 15 June, runs until 1 September at 11pm BST — three weeks remain for clubs to do business, with defending champions Arsenal and the rest still active in the market.

stories.headline: France Crowned 2026 Six Nations Champions in a 48-46 Thriller — England's Heartbreak as Nations Championship Era Begins
stories.summary: France retained the Six Nations title in dramatic fashion, winning the final match against England 48–46 courtesy of a last-gasp Thomas Ramos penalty, who also finished as the tournament's top scorer with 74 points. Louis Bielle-Biarrey was named Player of the Tournament after scoring nine tries — a new Six Nations record. Meanwhile, the Six Nations organisation has launched the new 'Nations Championship' era, which it describes as erasing old northern/southern hemisphere boundaries in global rugby.

stories.headline: Total Solar Eclipse One Week Away — Path Crosses Greenland, Iceland and Spain on 12 August
stories.summary: Space enthusiasts in the UK and across Europe are counting down to the total solar eclipse on 12 August 2026, visible in totality across northern Russia, Greenland, Iceland, and northern Spain. UK observers will see only a partial eclipse, but the event is being billed as one of the most accessible in decades for European audiences. NASA and Space.com have launched live coverage countdowns with expert updates ahead of eclipse day.

stories.headline: The Agentic AI Agent Guide: Delegate, Iterate, and Actually Learn
stories.summary: Ethan Mollick's July 31 piece in Forbes distills the key shift from chatbot-era AI to autonomous agents — arguing that the real unlock is delegating substantive real-world tasks and treating AI as a collaborator that requires direction and iteration rather than constant supervision. Mollick notes that agents can now autonomously handle hours of knowledge work, and the practical entry point is simply assigning a premium model a genuine task from your real workflow. For D&B, this validates the agentic archetype thesis entirely: as more professionals delegate prospecting, account research, and pipeline monitoring to agents, the quality of the structured data those agents draw on becomes the rate-limiting variable. D&B's entity resolution and temporal signals are precisely what separates an agent that surfaces noise from one that surfaces ground truth.
stories.source: Ethan Mollick (Wharton / One Useful Thing), Forbes, July 31 2026

stories.headline: Trust and Lock-In Are Now the Two Axes That Define Every Enterprise AI Vendor Decision
stories.summary: Kai Waehner's Enterprise Agentic AI Landscape Q2 2026 maps every major AI vendor — Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, AWS, OpenAI, Meta, Salesforce, SAP, Databricks, Cohere and others — across two dimensions that enterprises actually care about: how much they trust the vendor's AI, and how much lock-in they're prepared to accept. The core argument is that a model trustworthy for summarisation introduces entirely different risks when it operates autonomously making decisions, which means vendor choice is now an architectural and governance decision, not just a capability one. This is highly relevant to D&B's positioning: a neutral data layer embedded across all agentic platforms sidesteps the lock-in trap entirely, and D&B's explainability-first approach (Paydex, DUNS, verified entity resolution) directly addresses the trust axis that enterprises are struggling with. The 'be everywhere' / Visa neutrality analogy is the right counter-positioning to vendor-specific AI ecosystems.
stories.source: Kai Waehner (Independent Enterprise AI Analyst), kai-waehner.de, late July 2026

stories.headline: 2026 State of AI Agents: Multi-Agent Systems Grew 327% in Four Months — But Governance Is the Gap
stories.summary: Databricks' 2026 State of AI Agents report, drawing on data from over 20,000 organisations including more than 60% of the Fortune 500, finds that enterprises are rapidly transitioning from single chatbots to multi-agent systems — with adoption of those architectures growing 327% in under four months. The report flags that companies using evaluation tools get nearly 6x more AI projects into production, and those using AI governance frameworks achieve over 12x that rate, making governance infrastructure the clearest differentiator between organisations that ship and those that stall. For D&B, this is a direct commercial signal: multi-agent systems running across sales, procurement, and finance workflows need trusted, governed data inputs at every decision node, and the fragmentation of agent orchestration across platforms makes a neutral, verified data layer more valuable, not less. D&B's DUNS-anchored entity resolution and corporate family trees are exactly the kind of stable ground truth that prevents multi-agent drift and hallucination in production.

data_science.topic: Causal Inference — Moving from Correlation to Causation
data_science.tagline: Knowing that two things move together is table stakes. Knowing which one drives the other is where decisions get made.
data_science.what_it_is: Causal inference is the discipline of estimating the effect of an intervention — a treatment, a policy change, a product feature — on an outcome, using observational data where you can't run a clean randomized experiment. It sits at the intersection of statistics, economics, and machine learning. The core problem it solves: correlation is cheap and everywhere; causation is rare and actionable. If D&B signals correlate with churn, that's interesting. If those signals *cause* churn — or more precisely, if acting on them prevents churn — that's a product. The foundational framework is the Potential Outcomes model (Rubin Causal Model): for every unit (a business, a deal, a customer), we ask 'what would have happened if we had treated them differently?' The catch is that you only ever observe one outcome — the one that actually occurred. The counterfactual is missing by definition. Causal inference is a set of principled methods to estimate that missing counterfactual without randomization.
data_science.how_it_works: The toolkit has several major instruments, each suited to different data situations. (1) Propensity Score Matching / Weighting (IPW): Estimate the probability that a unit received treatment given its observable characteristics — the propensity score. Then match treated and control units with similar scores, or reweight the sample so the two groups look balanced. This mimics the balance you would have gotten from randomization. The danger: unmeasured confounders still bias results. (2) Difference-in-Differences (DiD): Compare the change in outcomes before and after a treatment for the treated group against the same change for a control group that did not receive treatment. The parallel trends assumption — that both groups would have moved together absent the treatment — is the load-bearing assumption. Staggered DiD (where different units adopt treatment at different times) is increasingly common and requires careful implementation (Callaway-Sant'Anna or Sun-Abraham estimators) to avoid negative weighting artifacts from the classic two-way fixed effects regression. (3) Instrumental Variables (IV): Find a variable (the instrument) that affects treatment assignment but has no direct path to the outcome except through the treatment. Classic example: lottery assignment as an instrument for program participation. IV gives you a Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) — the causal effect for compliers. Finding valid instruments is hard; weak instruments introduce large variance. (4) Regression Discontinuity (RD): Exploit a sharp threshold rule — e.g., a credit score cutoff that determines loan approval — to compare units just above and just below the cutoff. Near the threshold, assignment is essentially random. Gives clean local causal estimates but only at the threshold. (5) Causal ML / Double Machine Learning (DML): Use ML models to partial out the effect of high-dimensional confounders from both the treatment and outcome equations, then estimate the treatment effect on the residuals. Developed by Chernozhukov et al. Packages like EconML and DoubleML implement this. This is the modern bridge between causal inference and ML — you get the flexibility of gradient boosting or neural nets for nuisance functions, combined with rigorous causal identification. (6) Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs): A graphical language (from Judea Pearl) for encoding assumptions about causal structure. Nodes are variables; directed edges are causal relationships. DAGs let you identify which variables you must condition on (confounders), which you must not condition on (colliders, mediators), and whether your estimand is identified at all from your data. Tools: dagitty, CausalNex, DoWhy.
data_science.when_to_use: Use causal inference when a business decision hinges on intervention — not just prediction. Specifically: (1) You want to know whether doing X to a customer changes outcome Y, not just whether X and Y co-occur. (2) You cannot or should not run an A/B test — ethical constraints, one-time policy changes, historical retrospective analysis, or situations where the control arm is economically unacceptable. (3) You need to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects — not just the average effect, but who benefits most. (4) You are building a targeting or prioritization model and you want to rank by *uplift* (causal gain from treatment) rather than by raw outcome probability — a critical distinction. Targeting the people most likely to buy regardless of your action wastes budget. You want people whose behavior would change because of your action. Causal inference is NOT the right tool when: you genuinely have randomization (just use a t-test or regression); you only care about prediction with no intervention planned; your data is so thin that you cannot even reliably estimate propensity scores.
data_science.worked_example: D&B Scenario — Measuring the true lift of a Paydex alert on retention actions. D&B's customer success team sends proactive outreach (a retention call + discount offer) when a client's key supplier shows a Paydex deterioration signal. The business question: does that outreach actually cause retention, or do we just happen to call accounts that would have renewed anyway? You cannot randomize — withholding outreach from at-risk accounts is not acceptable. This is a classic causal inference problem on observational data. Step 1 — Build a DAG. Nodes: Paydex alert (trigger), account health score (confounder — sicker accounts get both alerts and calls), outreach received (treatment), and renewal at 90 days (outcome). The DAG reveals account health is a backdoor path you must block. Step 2 — Propensity Score Estimation. Train an XGBoost model to predict probability of receiving outreach given: account health score, company size, industry, contract value, prior Paydex history, days to renewal. This is your propensity score. Step 3 — Inverse Probability Weighting. Upweight accounts that received outreach despite low propensity (surprising treatments) and downweight those that received it despite high propensity (expected treatments). Now your treated and control groups are balanced on observables. Step 4 — Estimate the ATE. In the reweighted sample, run a regression of renewal on treatment indicator. The coefficient is your Average Treatment Effect — e.g., 'outreach causes a 9 percentage point increase in 90-day renewal probability.' Step 5 — Heterogeneous Treatment Effects with Causal Forest (via EconML). Fit a Causal Forest to estimate individualized treatment effects (CATE) by account segment. Finding: the effect is concentrated in mid-market accounts with Paydex alerts on tier-1 suppliers — small accounts and enterprise accounts show near-zero lift. Step 6 — Rewrite the targeting rule. Rather than triggering outreach on any Paydex alert, the model now scores each at-risk account by predicted CATE. The top quartile by uplift gets the expensive retention call; the rest get an automated email. This is uplift modeling — and it's only possible because you did causal inference, not just predictive scoring. The business impact: same outreach budget, materially better retention outcomes, because you stopped 'treating' accounts that would have renewed regardless. This is exactly the kind of explainability-first, ground-truth reasoning that underpins D&B's AI Decision Intelligence positioning — agents that don't just predict churn probability but prescribe interventions to the accounts where action actually changes the trajectory.

'The Book of Why' by Judea Pearl & Dana Mackenzie — conceptual foundation for DAGs and the do-calculus, essential reading for understanding what causal questions are even asking
